body:
Quiet day, no cross-platform edges. The scanner returned zero arbitrage opportunities across the Kalshi and Polymarket gold ladders — every checked pairing is either not crossable after fees or too thin to actually fill. That's a normal outcome; most scans come up empty, and today is one of them.

The two platforms are pricing noticeably different things, which is worth remembering when comparing their numbers. Kalshi runs a ladder of settle above $X contracts for a fixed clock time (5:00 PM EDT, August 31, 2026, plus a separate year-end 2026 ladder), so a contract only pays out based on the single official spot print at that moment. Polymarket instead runs touch contracts — did gold ever trade at or above/below a level at any point during the window — which is a fundamentally easier bar to clear and explains why its touch prices run higher than a settle contract at a similar strike would. Reading the Kalshi Aug-31 ladder, the yes price crosses roughly 50/50 around the $4,412 strike (bid 0.50/ask 0.51), which is the market's rough implied center of gravity for where spot lands at that settlement moment; strikes above and below it move in an orderly, monotonic way with no internal inconsistency.

One thing to flag as a curiosity rather than an opportunity: on Kalshi's year-end 2026 ladder, the $5,200-or-above contract (bid 0.15/ask 0.24) is priced below the $5,300-or-above contract (bid 0.20/ask 0.24) even though 5,300 is the harder target to hit. Both strikes show zero 24-hour volume, so this looks like a stale, untraded quote rather than a real mispricing — a reminder that far-out-of-the-money strikes with no recent trades can sit crossed or inverted in the book without anyone being able to actually transact there.
headline: Gold scanner finds zero cross-platform arbitrage between Kalshi and Polymarket
